title: Integral refinement pasting for the prescribed normalized maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness of the schemes is imposed. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories $C_s(T)=D^b_{ctf}(T,s)$ [def-sf-categories], completed at integral stages and with positive finite levels $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\ge1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Fix $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$. For each compactification $c=(j_c,p_c)$ write $B_c=S_{p_c}J_{j_c}$ on the ordinary derived categories of strict semilinear $(A_n)_T$-module systems, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total limit. Use the specified intrinsic proper/open maps and direct-image compositors of [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting], and their normalized integral realizations $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Assume the reduced inputs and all intermediate systems in every identity or binary refinement diagram are normalized, uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, so that these realization isomorphisms apply.

Let $F_c:C_R(X)\to C_R(Y)$ be integral compact-support functors with full inclusions $I_T$ into the ordinary completed-ring derived category and realizations $r_c:I_YF_c\cong Rp_{c,*}j_{c!}I_X$, compatible with the prescribed integral compact-support realization [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For every proper refinement $u:c\to d$ give an isomorphism $\rho_u:F_c\cong F_d$ with the following ringed-site normalization. After conjugation by $r_c,r_d$ it is the proper-composition map followed by $Rp_{d,*}(e_u^{-1})$. Here $e_u:j_{d!}\cong Ru_*j_{c!}$ is characterized by its open-adjunction transpose: composing that transpose with the canonical open-restriction/clopen-section isomorphism gives the open unit. Compactifications and refinements are those of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

Then the given integral maps satisfy
$$\rho_{1_c}=1_{F_c},\qquad\rho_{vu}=\rho_v\rho_u.$$
More precisely the ordinary derived image of $\rho_u$, after the prescribed realizations, is the total-limit image of the intrinsic system refinement map $B_c\to B_d$. This equality is compatible with whiskering by the proper and open factors appearing in the same diagram. It identifies actual integral morphisms and their compositors before any finite evaluation; equality of evaluated arrows alone is not a hypothesis for this conclusion.

proof.text: For $u:c\to d$ use its square $(k,i,r,p)=(j_c,j_d,1_X,u)$ and write $g_u:J_{j_d}\to S_uJ_{j_c}$ for $\Gamma_Q$. The compactification definition gives $uj_c=j_d$ and $p_du=p_c$. The intrinsic transpose formula of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting] gives $\lambda_uP_{j_d}g_u=1$. Its vertical pasting and [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting] give $g_{vu}=c_{v,u}(S_vg_u)g_v$ and $g_{1_c}=1$, with the prescribed direct-image compositors $c$. These are equations of system transformations before evaluation.

proof.text: Realize $g_u$ using [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. The generator statement [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence] identifies its integral map with the open-adjunction transpose of inverse open restriction through the clopen component. Its transpose is therefore $\lambda_u^{-1}$ times the open unit. This is precisely the defining transpose of the supplied $e_u$. Injectivity of the open-adjunction Hom bijection gives equality with $e_u$, not merely equality of finite evaluations. The same realization intertwines the proper compositors. All inputs and intermediate systems here meet the normalized, origin and common-bound assumptions by hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); agent assembly on normalized integral systems using the cited realization theorems.

proof.text: Consequently $\mathcal L(g_u)$ is invertible on the indicated systems, since it is conjugate to $e_u$. For its normalized source $M$ and target $N$, [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] supplies invertible actual counits $e_M,e_N$. Counit naturality reads $g_ue_M=e_N\mathcal R\mathcal L(g_u)$, so $g_u=e_N\mathcal R\mathcal L(g_u)e_M^{-1}$ is invertible as a system map. Thus put $t_u=(S_{p_d}g_u^{-1})c_{p_d,u}^{-1}:B_c\to B_d$. Here and below all compositors are evaluated on the displayed open-extension inputs.

proof.text: Invert the equation of Step 1: $g_{vu}^{-1}=g_v^{-1}(S_vg_u^{-1})c_{v,u}^{-1}$. In $t_vt_u$, naturality moves $c_{p_e,v}^{-1}$ past $S_{p_d}(g_u^{-1})$, where $p_d=p_ev$. Associativity of $c$ then identifies the two inverse compositors with $(S_{p_e}c_{v,u}^{-1})c_{p_e,vu}^{-1}$. Hence $t_vt_u=S_{p_e}(g_v^{-1}(S_vg_u^{-1})c_{v,u}^{-1})c_{p_e,vu}^{-1}=t_{vu}$. The identity equation follows from $g_1=1$ and the unital compositor. These are identities on the assumed diagram domain.

proof.text: For an integral input $K$ write $\bar c_{B_c}$ for $c_{B_c}$ followed by the prescribed compact-support realization into $Rp_{c,*}j_{c!}I_X$, and set $a_c=r_c^{-1}\bar c_{B_c}:\mathcal L B_c\mathcal R K\to I_YF_cK$, with the ambient inclusions understood. By Step 2 and the prescribed ringed-site normalization of $\rho_u$, the realization theorem gives $I_Y(\rho_u)=a_d\mathcal L(t_u)a_c^{-1}$. Its clause on whiskering gives this same equality with every permitted proper/open outer factor and the same compositors; inverses are respected because the generator maps are invertible on this domain. Apply $\mathcal L$ to Step 4. Substitution cancels $a_d^{-1}a_d$ and yields $I_Y(\rho_v\rho_u)=a_e\mathcal L(t_vt_u)a_c^{-1}=I_Y(\rho_{vu})$, and $I_Y(\rho_1)=1$. Faithfulness of the full inclusion gives both asserted integral laws. Zero inputs and empty opens give the unique zero-object arrows; for identity refinements the same formulas use only unitors. No argument detects equality by finite evaluation.
